result.title: ORDO: Fine-Grained Motion Understanding in Video LLMs via Order-Dependent Supervision
result.comment: 16 pages, 5 figures, 9 tables. Includes supplementary material
result.summary: Video large language models (video LLMs) answer a wide range of questions about real videos, yet they remain weak at fine-grained motion such as whether an object speeds up or slows down. Existing methods train these models on synthetic motion clips, on order pretext tasks such as reordering shuffled clips, or with rewards that compare ordered and perturbed frames. None of them requires that the label be unrecoverable from the frames once their order is discarded, so a model can fit such data from static cues without learning to use frame order. We propose ORDO, a framework that builds this requirement into the training data. We define order-necessary supervision as data in which the unordered set of frames has the same distribution under competing labels, and we realise it for motion attributes with three constructions, time-reversal pairing, matched spatial extent and uniform interval coverage. A procedural curriculum of six motion primitives instantiates these constructions, and low-rank adapters of the language model are trained on it with an answer-level objective and self-distillation replay on real videos. With 4,000 synthetic clips, ORDO raises the mean accuracy over four motion benchmarks by +7.6, +4.9 and +5.1 points on Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3-VL-8B and Molmo2-8B, while the same training with shuffled frames changes it by less than one point. Code and generator will be made publicly available.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ORDO 框架，通过时间反转配对、匹配空间范围等构造使标签在打乱帧序后不可恢复的「顺序必要监督」，配合六种运动原语的课程数据，对视频 LLM 的 LoRA 做答案级训练与真实视频自蒸馏回放，提升细粒度运动理解。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「丢弃顺序后标签分布不变」的数据构造思路，可能为核查 latent 推理状态是否真正使用视觉证据、而非从静态线索走旁路提供可借鉴的监督与诊断设计，值得进一步确认。
